newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish air cargo exports half Nordic total - report.
newsitem.headline: Swedish air cargo exports half Nordic total - report.

text.p: Swedish exports were behind almost half the Nordic region's outbound air cargo traffic in 1995, or 117,900 tonnes, a recent report commissioned by regional aviation administrations here showed.

Export air cargo volumes in 1995 from the Nordic region totalled 253,500 tonnes, said the report, compiled on behalf of Swedish and Finnish civil aviation authorities, New Oslo Airport Gardermoen and Copenhagen Airports.
Of the total, Sweden accounted for 47 percent, Denmark 22 percent, Norway 17 percent and Finland the remaining 14 percent.

The biggest destination for cargo from this part of the world was the Far East, with 35.6 percent of the total ending up there. Next largest were air cargo exports to North America, at 22.6 percent, followed by Europe at 19.9 percent.
Exports to Latin America by air were third highest at 7.3 percent. No comparison figures for 1994 were available.
Swedish exports to the Far East accounted for 28.2 percent, an increase of 45.5 percent from 1994, the report said. Exports to China from Sweden by air soared by over 100 percent.

Second largest for Swedish exports was North America, at 25.6 percent, which was a touch lower or 0.5 percent below 1994 levels, the report said. To Europe, air cargo exports were steady at 16.2 percent.
To Latin America, 10.3 percent of the pie, exports rose 13.3 percent with South America jumping 28.9 percent.

Air exports from Denmark to the Far East totalled 27.5 percent and to Europe, 20.2 percent. From Norway, 58.8 percent of air cargo exports were to the Far East, with 17,610 tonnes of the Far Eastern total of 27,450 tonnes going to Japan.
From Finland, European air exports were highest at 31.1 percent followed by the Far East at 29.3 percent.
